items.title: Google Says Links Will Be More Visible In AI Overviews
items.summary: Google is updating AI Overviews and AI Mode to make links more visible by adding hover pop-ups on desktop that show site names, favicons, and descriptions, and by using more descriptive link icons on desktop and mobile. This change aims to make it easier for users to access content from the web, addressing concerns about reduced click-through rates to publisher sites due to AI summaries. The update is part of ongoing efforts to improve link visibility in AI-generated responses, benefiting SEO by potentially increasing traffic from AI search.

items.title: Enterprise SEO Operating Models That Scale In 2026 And Beyond
items.summary: Enterprises must redesign SEO operating models around eligibility, governance, and structural clarity to succeed in AI-driven search, treating SEO as organizational infrastructure rather than just marketing. Visibility now hinges on upstream intent modeling, taxonomy, and cross-functional accountability instead of post-launch tweaks. This shift requires integrating SEO into core systems for machine-readable clarity, aligning content strategies with Google algorithm changes and AI search demands.

items.title: Google releases February 2026 Discover core update
items.summary: Google has released the February 2026 Discover core update, prioritizing locally relevant content from websites based in a user's country, reducing sensational and clickbait content, and highlighting in-depth, original, and timely content from expert sites. The update rolls out first to English-language users in the U.S. and will expand globally, potentially causing traffic fluctuations in Google Discover. SEO and content marketers should focus on local relevance, topic expertise, and quality content to maintain visibility.

items.title: Google's February 2026 Discover Core Update
items.summary: Google released a broad February 2026 Discover core update to improve user experience by surfacing more locally relevant content, reducing sensationalism and clickbait, and prioritizing in-depth, original, timely content from expert sites on a topic basis. It may cause traffic changes for some publishers, starting with U.S. English users before global rollout. Publishers should align with core update guidance and Discover best practices for sustained visibility in personalized feeds.

items.title: AI didn't kill SEO. It killed average content.
items.summary: Generative AI has not eliminated SEO but has raised the bar by standardizing what distinguishes high-quality from low-quality content, making exceptional content marketing essential for success. Strategies must now emphasize uniqueness, depth, and value to stand out in AI-influenced search environments. This trend underscores the need for content creators to move beyond average output toward innovative, user-focused approaches amid evolving algorithms.

items.title: MURDER DRONES: THE OFFICIAL GRAPHIC NOVEL Crowdfunding Triumph
items.summary: Oni Press's Kickstarter for the official graphic novel of the hit animated series Murder Drones has smashed records, raising $1.8 million from over 21,000 backers. The 136-page collection by Wyatt Kennedy and Jo Mi-Gyeong features drone horror on exoplanet Copper 9 with behind-the-scenes extras. items.title: Daniel Radcliffe Praises New 'Harry Potter' HBO Lead Dominic McLaughlin
items.summary: Daniel Radcliffe has endorsed the new HBO adaptation of the Harry Potter series, predicting that lead actor Dominic McLaughlin 'is going to be better than me' in the role he originated. Speaking ahead of the eight-season series' 2027 premiere, Radcliffe asked the media to avoid comparisons that could haunt the young new cast, stating, 'I would like not to be weird spectral phantoms in these children’s lives.' The comments come amid ongoing buzz for the faithful book-to-screen retelling.

items.title: Kristen Bell Joins 'Sonic the Hedgehog 4' Voice Cast as Amy Rose
items.summary: Kristen Bell is set to voice Amy Rose in Paramount's Sonic the Hedgehog 4, joining returning stars Ben Schwartz (Sonic), Idris Elba (Knuckles), and Keanu Reeves (Shadow). Directed by Jeff Fowler, the sci-fi adventure film features live-action reprises from Jim Carrey, James Marsden, and others, with a release date of March 19, 2027. The franchise continues its successful run adapting the beloved Sega video game series.

items.title: 'Wuthering Heights' Adaptation Opens Strong with $37.5M Domestic Box Office
items.summary: Emerald Fennell's star-studded take on Emily Brontë's classic novel Wuthering Heights, featuring Margot Robbie and Jacob Elordi, debuted with $37.5 million domestically and $83 million globally. The gothic romance topped the box office charts over the weekend, signaling strong audience interest in the literary adaptation. Critics note its bold, modern twist on the timeless story of passion and revenge.

items.title: Experts Pick Top 2026 Book-to-Film Adaptations: Project Hail Mary, The Odyssey, Narnia
items.summary: Among the most anticipated 2026 book adaptations are Andy Weir's sci-fi hit Project Hail Mary starring Ryan Gosling (March), Christopher Nolan's epic The Odyssey with Matt Damon (July), and C.S. Lewis' fantasy The Magician’s Nephew kicking off Greta Gerwig’s Narnia series (November). These projects highlight Hollywood's continued push into high-profile literary sci-fi and fantasy. Other notables include Helen Macdonald's H is for Hawk.

items.title: Entrepreneurs Can Improve Their Workflow With This AI E-Degree
items.summary: Nearly 50% of businesses are using AI for at least one function, and this ChatGPT and Automation E-Degree offers entrepreneurs a beginner-friendly way to integrate AI into their operations. The bundle includes 12 courses with 25 hours of instruction on practical AI tools like ChatGPT, automation for streamlining processes, and over 20 industry-tailored tools to enhance marketing, coding, and business efficiency. Priced at $19.99, it helps small business owners catch up on AI to save resources and future-proof their ventures.

items.title: By Year's End, 4 In 5 Small Businesses Will Use AI Marketing Tools
items.summary: By the end of 2026, over 80% of small businesses will adopt AI marketing tools, with 54% already using them for tasks like trend analysis, content creation, and image generation, enabling solopreneurs to access enterprise-level capabilities at low cost. This surge is driven by the need to boost customer engagement on channels like social media and email, where AI helps optimize campaigns amid rising marketing investments. However, small businesses must focus on adding unique human expertise to AI-generated content to stand out in a crowded market.

items.title: New Study Reveals Small-Business Enthusiasm for AI
items.summary: A study from the Connected Commerce Council reveals that 70% of small-business leaders have invested in or plan to adopt AI tools, with 55% noting increased employee productivity and 53% deeming AI critical to success. Among digital ad users, 72% report that AI simplifies campaign setup and enhances effectiveness, while 62% express excitement about AI's growth potential for their businesses. This highlights AI's role in boosting efficiency and competitiveness for small businesses, though 59% warn they might abandon tools if costs or regulations rise.

items.title: New Report: Small Businesses Enter 2026 with Sustained Confidence
items.summary: Small business owners are entering 2026 with high confidence, as 94% project growth amid challenges like inflation and cash flow. AI adoption is growing, with 56% of businesses using it primarily for marketing, and 87% of AI users reporting positive impacts on their operations. This highlights opportunities for small businesses to leverage AI tools for efficiency and strategic planning while accessing non-bank lenders for capital needs.
